topic: A wedding card arrives from a haveli that has been locked for fifty years.

episode.title: Midnight Watch: The Wedding Invitation

shots.narration: That wedding card came from a haveli locked fifty years.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, 3D animated Pakistani village courtyard at night; Bashir and Saad beside a brass lantern, blank ivory wedding card with red ribbon between them, no lettering.
shots.action: Bashir holds the wedding card toward Saad.
shots.mood: Warm lantern glow against cold fog, deep courtyard shadows.

shots.narration: Bashir told Saad what happened when he accepted.
shots.scene: Same moonlit courtyard; grey-bearded Bashir in brown woollen shawl and white cap faces Saad in a dark green hoodie and jeans.
shots.action: Bashir points toward a distant shuttered haveli.
shots.mood: Quiet anticipation, distant building barely visible through mist.

shots.narration: [whispers] The ribbon slipped off before I touched the gate.
shots.scene: Earlier that night outside the old haveli; Bashir holds his brass lantern and blank wedding card before a chained wooden gate.
shots.action: The red ribbon slides off Bashir's card.
shots.mood: Silver moonlight, dusty wood, unnatural stillness.

shots.narration: Then the lock opened all by itself.
shots.scene: Close view of a huge rusty padlock on the haveli gate, Bashir visible behind it with his lantern.
shots.mood: Sharp brass highlights, black gaps between wooden planks.

shots.narration: Inside, fresh wedding flowers covered fifty years of dust.
shots.scene: Haveli entrance opening onto a dusty courtyard decorated with fresh marigold garlands, no people or writing anywhere.
shots.mood: Bright orange flowers against neglected stone and thick cobwebs.

shots.narration: [surprised] One wedding chair faced the door, waiting.
shots.scene: Empty haveli wedding courtyard; a single carved chair with red cushions stands beneath marigold garlands, Bashir near the entrance.
shots.action: Bashir raises his lantern toward the chair.
shots.mood: Lonely ceremonial grandeur, darkness pooling beneath the seat.

shots.narration: I left the invitation there instead.
shots.scene: Beside the carved wedding chair, its red cushion thick with dust; Bashir's lantern lights the blank ivory card.
shots.action: Bashir places the card on the cushion.
shots.mood: Careful hesitation, warm light surrounded by empty darkness.

shots.narration: The doors closed before I could leave.
shots.scene: Interior view toward the haveli's tall wooden entrance doors, Bashir standing between the doorway and wedding chair.
shots.mood: Sudden enclosure, thinning moonlight, heavy architectural shadows.

shots.narration: [whispers] My lantern still burned, but my shadow was gone.
shots.scene: Dusty courtyard floor around Bashir; his brass lantern casts clear chair shadows, but none beneath his feet.
shots.action: Bashir lowers his lantern toward the floor.
shots.mood: Impossible absence, small golden light, vast dark courtyard.

shots.narration: Then the empty chair scraped toward me.
shots.scene: Wedding courtyard with Bashir standing rigid before the red-cushioned chair, blank card still on its seat.
shots.action: The chair slides across the dusty floor toward Bashir.
shots.mood: Narrowing distance, disturbed dust, oppressive silence.

shots.narration: My shadow sat down, but I was still standing.
shots.scene: Bashir stands beside the wedding chair; on the pale wall behind it, his unmistakable cap-and-shawl shadow is upright and detached from him.
shots.action: Bashir's detached shadow folds into a seated pose behind the empty chair.
shots.mood: Darkest moment, enormous black silhouette, trembling lantern glow.

shots.narration: [whispers] Now, Saad, why does your invitation show the abandoned station?
shots.scene: Back in the village courtyard beside Bashir's lantern; Saad holds the ivory card, its reverse embossed with a railway platform and clock, without letters or numbers.
shots.action: Saad turns the card over to reveal the railway image.
shots.mood: Familiar lantern warmth turned uneasy, railway image catching cold moonlight.

episode.endHook: Why does the wedding card now show an abandoned railway station?
episode.description: A wedding card arrives from a Pakistani haveli locked for fifty years. Beside his lantern, Bashir Chacha tells Saad why one seat at that wedding was never empty. A fictional spooky story from Midnight Watch.
